items.title: Korea’s leverage trap has an echo in India
items.description: Indian brokers are lending large sums to retail investors, creating systemic risk.  Retail investors are borrowing heavily to buy stocks at stretched valuations.  This margin debt has ballooned significantly, with new-age brokers aggressively competing.  Unlike Korea's AI focus, India's debt supports stocks global investors are avoiding.  Policymakers face challenges as inflation and a weakening rupee test their resolve.

items.title: Sebi opens faster route for rollout of AIF plans
items.description: The Securities and Exchange Board of India has introduced a new green channel mechanism. This new framework, called GARUDA, aims to speed up the launch of Alternative Investment Fund schemes. Regular AIF schemes can now be launched ten days after filing their placement memorandum. Accredited investor only funds and large value funds have been granted further flexibility. These changes will allow for quicker introduction of new AIF plans.

items.title: Sebi agrees to settle all NSE cases, clears way for mega IPO
items.description: India's National Stock Exchange has settled all pending regulatory cases for a significant sum. This settlement clears the final major hurdle for the exchange's long-delayed stock market debut. The Securities and Exchange Board of India agreed to the settlement terms after years of legal battles. NSE plans to raise over twenty-six thousand crore rupees this year. The financial impact of the settlement has already been accounted for.

items.title: NSE Q1 profit up 8.7% at Rs 3,120 crore
items.description: The National Stock Exchange reported a profit after tax of ₹3,120 crore for the June quarter. This represents an increase of 8.7% from the previous quarter's earnings. Consolidated revenue from operations saw a decline of 8.2% compared to the prior quarter. Year-on-year, the consolidated profit after tax rose by 7%. Meanwhile, consolidated revenue from operations increased by 13% from the same period last year.

items.title: These large- and mid-cap stocks can give more than 25% return in 1 year, according to analysts
items.description: The price of crude oil is down again despite the escalating tensions in the Gulf region. That augurs well for markets. This does not mean that corrections will not happen; they will. But, largely, they will have a lesser probability of turning into a secular bearish trend as has happened in the past.  Mind you, we are using the word probability. Why?

items.title: Brokerages raise Asian Paints price targets after strong Q1 earnings, but retain cautious stance
items.description: Brokerages increased price targets for Asian Paints after strong June quarter earnings. Most analysts maintained their existing recommendations for the paint company. Rich valuations and rising raw material costs limit the stock's upside potential. Intense competition also continues to affect the company's performance. Analysts' consensus price target suggests a ten percent upside from Thursday's close.

items.title: Pre-market action: Here's the trade setup for today's session
items.description: Indian benchmark indices opened flat and traded in a choppy, volatile range. Analysts suggest the index may head towards resistance at 24,500-24,600 levels. The India VIX, measuring market fear, rose 1.2% to settle at 12.16. Foreign portfolio investors and domestic institutions were net buyers of shares on Thursday. The Indian rupee closed nearly flat, blunting pressure from oil prices and corporate demand.

items.title: Stocks in news: Maruti Suzuki, ITC, Vedanta, Swiggy, RIL
items.description: Indian markets traded in a narrow range, settling marginally higher with mixed cues. Maruti Suzuki, ITC, and Vedanta shares are in focus due to various news developments. Sun Pharma and Bajaj Finserv will announce their first quarter results today. Tata Steel reported a fifteen percent rise in its net profit for the June quarter. Reliance Industries ramped up diesel exports to Europe and Brazil in July.

items.title: State insurers quote low premiums to win NPCIL nuke insurance cover
items.description: Nuclear Power Corp of India (NPCIL) had budgeted Rs 30.13 crore, including taxes, for insuring Tarapur units 3 and 4 under a one-year property damage programme, said sources. The reverse auction for covering the risk, however, saw bids fall dramatically, with Oriental Insurance quoting Rs 10 crore, United India Insurance Rs 10.98 crore, and New India Assurance Rs 28.9 crore, they added.

items.title: Mid-tier private banks rake in more low-cost deposits
items.description: "Our Casa was only 10% initially. For the first three or four years of taking over management of this bank, we slowed down the loan book and focused on building the Casa ratio to 50%," V Vaidyanathan, MD and CEO, IDFC First Bank, told ET in an interview. "If we had kept growing the loan book, we could never have addressed structural issues like this. I believe in playing the long game in every format."

items.title: FCNR(B) hurdle: Singapore holds ground on withholding tax
items.description: Given the spread between interest offered on FCNR deposits and interest charged on loans, a 10% WTH on loan interest on tax grossed-up basis would erase effective returns. Where spreads are thin and final yield is generated through higher leverage, the tax can result in negative return.

items.title: Multibagger Astra Microwave shares rally 14% to 52-week high after Rs 2,205 crore order win from HAL
items.description: Astra Microwave Products shares surged 14% to a fresh 52-week high of Rs 1,960 after securing a massive Rs 2,205 crore order from Hindustan Aeronautics (HAL) for Uttam Radar components. The five-year contract nearly doubles the company's existing order book, driving strong buying interest in the multibagger defence stock.

items.title: Vedanta share price target: Why brokerages see up to 24% upside after Q1 earnings?
items.description: Vedanta's net profit surged 72% year-on-year to Rs 5,473 crore. EBITDA also jumped 98% to a record Rs 8,469 crore. The company announced Arun Misra as its new CEO, effective August first. Nuvama maintained a buy rating with a target price of Rs 333. Motilal Oswal maintained its Neutral rating on Vedanta shares with a target price of Rs 290 apiece, implying 8% upside potential.

items.title: Meesho among 3 stocks that closed above VWAP, signaling bullish shift
items.description: On July 30, the closing prices of three stocks in the Nifty500 pack rallied over 1.5% relative to their VWAP (Volume Weighted Average Price). A shift above the VWAP suggests a potential bullish trend, according to stockedge.com's technical scan data.When the closing price rises above the VWAP, it signifies that the closing price is higher than the average price at which it was traded throughout the day, with the average being weighted by trading volume. This occurrence is often interpreted as a potential bullish signal by traders and investors. This potentially indicates positive sentiment in the market.

items.title: Swiggy shares plunge 6% even as losses narrow. Should investors buy, sell or accumulate?
items.description: Swiggy shares plunged as much as 6% after the food delivery and quick commerce company reported its June-quarter results. While the consolidated net loss narrowed year-on-year, investors remained cautious over profitability and margin pressures. Brokerages stayed largely positive on the stock, with most retaining their 'Buy' ratings, citing long-term growth potential despite near-term challenges.

items.title: Bajaj Finance shares rally 5% after Q1 results. What Nomura, Nuvama, other brokerages expect
items.description: Bajaj Finance shares jumped after the NBFC reported a strong Q1 FY27 performance, with standalone net profit rising 28% YoY to Rs 6,081 crore and net interest income growing 23% to Rs 12,571 crore. Robust earnings prompted several brokerages to raise their target prices. The company's assets under management increased by Rs 36,969 crore, while new loan bookings rose 20% to 16.13 million.

items.title: M&M shares climb 3% after strong Q1 results. Morgan Stanley sees up to 29% upside scope
items.description: Mahindra & Mahindra shares climbed up to 3% after the automaker reported a 7% year-on-year rise in standalone net profit to Rs 3,685 crore for the June quarter. Revenue from operations surged 23% to Rs 41,920 crore, driven by robust demand. The strong quarterly performance lifted investor sentiment, pushing the stock to an intraday high of Rs 3,365.

items.title: Sensex rises over 50 points, Nifty above 24,350; Bajaj twins, M&M among top gainers
items.description: The Indian stock market extended gains on Friday as the Sensex rose 50 points and Nifty crossed 24,350 amid positive global cues. Bajaj Finance and M&M led gainers, while Nifty IT dragged. Strong FII inflows and stable earnings continue supporting market resilience, with technical charts signalling further upside towards 24,500.

items.title: Buy, Sell or Hold: Elara Capital downgrades Swiggy; Morgan Stanley remains overweight on M&M
items.description: Top brokerages issued fresh stock views following mixed Q1 FY27 earnings. Elara Capital downgraded Swiggy to Accumulate with a target of Rs 350 over delayed profitability. Morgan Stanley remained Overweight on M&M with a Rs 4,222 target, while Goldman Sachs kept a Neutral stance on Tata Steel at Rs 218.

items.title: Karnataka Bank among 4 stocks flashing bullish signals, hinting at a possible uptrend
items.description: On July 30, four NSE-listed stocks with a market capitalisation of over Rs 10,000 crore were identified by StockEdge’s ‘White Marubozu’ bullish scanner, according to technical scan data. A White Marubozu is a bullish candlestick pattern in technical analysis that occurs when the opening price is the lowest for a given period and the closing price is the highest.Represented by a long white (or green) candlestick with no upper shadow and a small or nonexistent lower shadow, it indicates strong buying pressure throughout the session. Traders interpret it as a signal that buyers were in control from the opening to the closing, often using such patterns for informed decisions about future price movements in financial markets.

items.title: From 87% to 51%: How Nifty50 companies lost their grip on India Inc's profits
items.description: Nifty 50 companies now contribute only 51% of aggregate profits, down from 87%. Earnings growth has accelerated across the broader Indian corporate universe and mid-sized firms. This shift signals a broadening wealth creation engine beyond just the largest companies. Financials have become the largest profit contributor, overtaking Energy sectors. Investors should consider portfolios beyond just mega-cap stocks for growth.

items.title: India's family offices embrace profit-sharing to attract top talent
items.description: India's family offices are increasingly adopting profit-sharing and carried interest models to attract and retain top investment talent as competition intensifies in the country's rapidly expanding wealth management industry. The shift reflects the growing number of family offices and rising demand for experienced investment professionals.

items.title: Sankaran Naren favours banks, power as oil risks loom
items.description: Sankaran Naren, CIO of ICICI Prudential Asset Management, remains bullish on banks, power utilities, oil refiners and pharmaceuticals, citing attractive valuations and improving earnings despite global uncertainties. He cautioned that a sharp rise in crude oil prices could weigh on market valuations even as corporate profits recover.

items.title: Balkrishna Industries among 4 stocks showing bullish RSI upswing
items.description: On July 30, four Nifty500 stocks that gained over 2% were highlighted in the RSI Trending Up scan, based on data from StockEdge.com. An uptrend signal is generated when the RSI value crosses above 50 from lower levels. “RSI trending up” indicates that Relative Strength Index (RSI) values are rising, suggesting strengthening momentum in the stock’s price action. This can indicate potential upward movement and is often used by traders to identify buying opportunities in momentum-driven markets.

items.title: Positive Breakout: These 10 stocks cross above their 200 DMAs
items.description: In the Nifty500 pack, 10 stocks' closing prices crossed above their 200 DMA (Daily Moving Averages) on July 30, 2026, according to stockedge.com's technical scan data. The 200-day daily moving average (DMA) is used by traders as a key indicator for determining the overall trend in a particular stock. As long as the stock is priced above the 200-day SMA on the daily timeframe, it is generally considered to be in an overall uptrend. Take a look:"

items.title: Bajaj Finance posts 28% growth in net profit amid healthy loan demand
items.description: Bajaj Finance reported a 28% year-on-year net profit increase for the June quarter.  Assets under management climbed 24% to ₹5.47 lakh crore as of June-end.  The company added 5.1 million new customers during the quarter.  Net interest income rose 23% and net total income increased 22%.  Bajaj Finance expects to disburse 60-62 million new loans in FY27.
